name: DJ Dahi
notes: Inglewood minimalism, and the parameter that carries it is negative space rather than any timbre. The research: "a small number of loud, well-separated hits … hats used sparingly or omitted entirely for whole sections. Swing is minimal; the groove comes from placement, not subdivision density." So this model is the parent with the density taken out — kick 2-3 a bar, ghost snares at 0.05, `hihat.continuous` false, percs at 0-1 a bar, and `swing.amount` back to a flat 0.50 against the lane's 0.52. ⚠ `hihat.fillDensity` is 0.30 rather than lower: with `continuous` false a model still owes every seed a hat, and below ~0.28 some seeds produce a bar with none. ⚠ The 808 is the loud element — `slideProb` 0.4 with a long `portamentoMs`, which is the research's "long, clean, low 808 with slow portamento … mixed as the loudest element after the vocal". ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is a description, not an exemption: the research says "a single sustained harmony or an `i–VII` alternation", so `maxChords` is 2 and the chord part's variety is carried by `chordDurationBeats` [4,16] and three harmonic rhythms rather than by families he does not play. ⚠ `halfStepDissonance` is high for this lane at 0.14 because the research names "dissonant sample residue left in rather than tuned out" — that residue is the model's one non-consonant parameter. ⚠ `medium`: the research rates him high-medium and says "specific gear unsourced". The INFERRED parameters are the kick's `secondaryAnchor` ("3a" is one reading of "one syncopated kick before the backbeat") and every humanize number. ⚠ The 130–150 half-time population the research documents is NOT modeled: `session.halfTime` is a single boolean and this entry authors no modes, so the band here is his 90–110 straight-2&4 population only. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 867 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 941/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 946/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.3 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 946/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
